text:
cheng: ran a multi-GPU nsys+perfetto capture to hunt a regression in TP=8 throughput. seeing repeated ~5-8ms tail spikes every step that line up with NCCL all-reduce start. KV cache churn looks suspicious too. attaching command and a tiny flame excerpt below. any quick ideas?

cheng: command i used:
```
nsys profile --output=prof_run1 --trace=cuda,nccl,osrt --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx:step_start,nvtx:step_end --stats=true 
```

cheng: flame excerpt (perfetto): host memcpy S->D spikes at same offsets as ncclAllReduce kickoffs, then a gap while kernels wait. also seeing kernel-selector pick a slower matmul path intermittently (same model, same seq len).

alex: can you paste the perfetto link or upload the .qdrep? :eyes:

cheng: uploaded: https://perfetto.dev/trace?e=abc123 (private)

maria: quick thought — are we hitting CPU-side packing for KV cache on rank 0? if the prefetcher is evicting and reloading, you'll see host->device memcpy spikes. how big are your KV pages?

cheng: KV page size is 64KB, cache capacity per-GPU ~2GB, but working set seems to briefly exceed due to batched prefixes, maybe fragmentation.

samir: also check the kernel selector logs — we've had a case where odd sequence-lengths triggered a non-fused attention kernel that serialized some streams. try enabling kernel debug env: `RL_RUNTIME_KERNEL_LOG=1` to confirm.

nidhi: NCCL side: are you using collReduceScatter->AllGather or a single AllReduce? overlap can be lost if timings force a serialized schedule. run with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and capture `nccl-tests` micro-run to see per-step schedule.

cheng: good call. nccl logs show small serialized allreduce windows on rank 3 occasionally. unclear why rank skew happens though.

alex: if it is skewed ranks, maybe OS scheduling. perfetto shows CPU scheduling gaps around the memcpy threads ~200-300us before the spike. could be a host thread backlog. try `taskset` to pin the runtime worker threads to cores with NVLINK interrupts offloaded.

maria: another quick repro: run 1 step with `RL_PREFETCHER=off` and one with `RL_PREFETCHER=on` to compare. if spikes go away with prefetcher off, prefetcher flush/rehydration is the culprit.

cheng: ran that: with prefetcher off the periodic spikes reduced but end-to-end latency increases a bit; with prefetcher on we get better avg but those nasty tails.

samir: sounds like prefetcher is over-eager and causes synchronous host memcpy when it hits a miss during an allreduce window. two mitigations: 1) make prefetcher async (background worker) or 2) delay allreduce start until KV handoff completes (we already have a handshake but it might be racy).

nidhi: also confirm NCCL version and libnuma pinning. older NCCL may fallback to CPU copy path for certain sizes. what driver + NCCL?

cheng: CUDA 12.1, driver 535.xx, NCCL 2.17.2. libnuma not explicitly pinned.

alex: try `numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0` for a short run as an experiment. also capture `perf record -a` for the host to see which syscall is blocking.

ops-bot: automated: uploaded prof_run1.nsys-rep to /mnt/profiles/2111112222/prof_run1.nsys-rep and generated perfetto link https://perfetto.dev/trace?e=abc123 (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

maria: if the kernel selector is flipping, we should log input shapes to confirm. can you grep the runtime logs for `Selector picked`? should be `Selector picked <kernel_id> for <shape>`; if it's alternating you might have nondeterministic cost model.

cheng: found alternating selector picks for attention kernel id 0x3a and 0x7f depending on tiny timing differences. attaching snippet:```
[2024-06-12 14:02:03] Selector picked kernel 0x3a for attn (seq=512, batch=4)
[2024-06-12 14:02:03.006] Selector picked kernel 0x7f for attn (seq=512, batch=4)
```

samir: that explains perf jitter — two kernels have different stream usage and one blocks an NCCL stream. we should bias the selector toward the lower-variance kernel for production. add a short-term guard: `RL_KERNEL_PREFER=0x3a` to test.

cheng: applied `RL_KERNEL_PREFER=0x3a` and re-ran one epoch: tails dropped ~60% on perfetto sample. nice.

nidhi: put together a small checklist to follow up:
- reproduce with numactl (alex)
- run NCCL microbench to confirm no unexpected CPU copies (nidhi)
- add selector bias and see stability (samir)
- evaluate making prefetcher async (maria)

cheng: i'll run the checklist tomorrow and create a tiny PR to set selector bias as a canary for the next rollout. thanks all :pray:
